title: metadata-protocol: a save into a second package of an object a runtime-authored row owns answers 200 while the registry refuses the ownership — `classifyObjectContribution` protects code owners only (ADR-0029 D9.9)
body:
Filing gate ①, class (b): a declared contract that a door breaks, measured at a public door. Filed by `domain:spec` seat 1 (#6017) · `huangyiirene` · session `session_01YRp5z4kK6vgYkrdH97ztsy`, from #23297's dev report (`os-dev-report` on #23297, out-of-scope finding 2; PR #23408). ⛔ Not a claim. Grade and lane are triage's.

`Seam: spec:ADR-0029 D9.9 (overlayPackageMismatchError) → runtime:ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.classifyObjectContribution (saveMetaItem) | consumer: the registry's registerObject ownership rule`

**Reader who acts:** triage, to grade and route. Then the owning seat. The landing point is `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` `classifyObjectContribution`.

## What happens (measured)

On a booted showcase at `main` `6eb6f7d65`, and again at the #23297 branch tree `ae6b35c16`:
1. Package `com.qa.p` saves the runtime-authored object `qa_probe_gadget`.
2. `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/qa_probe_gadget?package=com.qa.q` answers `200` "Saved object (env-wide, package=com.qa.q)".
3. The dev log prints a warn: `[Protocol] registerObject failed ... is already owned by package com.qa.p ... cannot claim ownership`.

The data plane keeps P's schema. So `sys_metadata` now describes a Q-bound shape the registry refused to hold.

## The contract

ADR-0029 D9.9, as the `overlayPackageMismatchError` docblock states it: refusing the mis-bound row "is what keeps the two stores in agreement instead of letting `sys_metadata` describe a shape the registry cannot hold". `classifyObjectContribution` asks only `getPackagedObjectOwner`, which answers for a code artifact (`isCodeArtifactBody`). So a runtime-authored owner is never protected, and the save answers `200` where the docblock says it refuses.

## What done looks like

- A save of an object owned by another package's runtime-authored row is refused, as a code-owned object's is, with the same prescription. The alternative is the owning seat measuring why a runtime owner must stay claimable, and saying so in that docblock.
- A pin on a real kernel. The negative control is that the owner package's own re-save still answers `200`.

## Family

#6995 (closed) is the same class, an object overlay silently discarded by `registerObject`'s ownership rule while `saveMetaItem` reports success. Its fix covered the code-packaged owner. This card is the runtime-authored owner.

## Dedupe

MCP `search_issues` on this repo, closed included: `runtime-authored object second package save 200 registerObject already owned classifyObjectContribution overlay package mismatch` gives 18 hits.
- #6995 (closed) is the code-owner case.
- #22220, #22128 and #23039 (closed) are other save-door or overlay-key defects.
- #18202, #12623, #12609 and #12789 are registry or validation questions on other axes.

None is this.

Dedupe words: registerObject already owned runtime object second package save 200; classifyObjectContribution runtime-authored owner; OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH runtime owner.
